newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia power firms social fund ready by June.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia power firms social fund ready by June.

text.p: A plan to make private power firms in Malaysia pay for the supply of power to rural areas will be finalised by June, Energy Minister Leo Moggie said on Monday.

The use of the social fund -- set up by independent power producers (IPPs) and state utility Tenaga Nasional for the rural electrification plan -- was being worked out, Moggie was quoted as saying by the national Bernama news agency.
"All electricity generators in the country, the IPPs and Tenaga Nasional have agreed to contribute to a cess fund established to support the activities in rural areas," he said.
Moggie did not reveal the size of the fund. But he said the parties involved have agreed on the percentage that IPPs had to contribute.

Tenaga, the sole provider of power to end-users in Malaysia, has always been responsible for setting up necessary infrastructure to supply power. But in recent years, the company has complained that such expenditure was cutting into its profits and suggested the IPPs share the cost.
Moggie said demand for power in Malaysia was growing at 14 percent a year.
Based on the current demand, national fossil fuel reserves could last another 15 years and natural gas another 70 years, he said. -- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-230 7509)
